instruction: Write a Kakoune script that defines a hidden command `mytool-status` which echoes the name of the current buffer.
Write a command `mytool-j` that moves the cursor down by one line, driving the editor through its normal key bindings.
note: Use execute-keys (runs keystrokes subject to mappings); `j` is the default move-down key.

instruction: Write a command `mytool-del` that moves down one line and deletes the anchored selection, running the delete directly so it is NOT affected by any user mapping of `delete-anchored`.
note: evaluate-commands runs the command directly, bypassing mappings; execute-keys drives the key j.

instruction: Write a command `mytool-escape` that echoes the literal text `%{foo}'bar` (a literal percent-brace and a literal single quote). Quote it correctly so Kakoune does not try to expand `%{foo}`.
note: Inside double quotes a doubled %% yields a literal %, so %%{foo} prints %{foo}; a single quote is literal inside double quotes.

instruction: Write a Kakoune script that declares a global boolean option `mytool-verbose` (default off) and a command `mytool-verbose-on` that turns it ON as a GLOBAL option, not a local one.
note: evaluate-commands inserts a local scope, so the option must be set with `set-option global`; wrap in -no-hooks to avoid hook noise. Option names allow only [a-zA-Z0-9_] (no hyphens), so `mytool-verbose` becomes `mytool_verbose`; boolean values are true/yes/false/no (not 0/1).

instruction: Write a script that adds a highlighter which colors every occurrence of the word TODO in red in the current buffer.
note: Use add-highlighter with a name, a regex, and an attribute; --override replaces any prior highlighter of the same name.

instruction: Write a script that runs a hook which echoes a message whenever a new buffer is created.
note: hook global binds to a global event; %val{bufname} expands to the new buffer's name at hook time.

instruction: Write a command `mytool-run` that shells out and prints the current directory using a POSIX-portable snippet (printf, not echo; $PWD, not $(pwd)).
note: Shell code inside %sh{} must be POSIX-portable: prefer printf over echo and $PWD over $(pwd).
A mismatched %{ is a parse error; every opening delimiter must be closed. Validate with scripts/kak-validate.sh.

instruction: Explain, in one sentence, what exit code `scripts/kak-validate.sh myscript.kak` returns when the script contains a runtime error such as `set buffer bogusoption 5`, and what the user sees on stderr.
ground_truth: It returns a non-zero exit code (1) and prints the Kakoune error message (with the leading `N:M: 'source': ` position prefix stripped) to stderr, so the user sees the exact reason it failed.
note: Validation is the final gate: non-zero on any load/runtime error, zero only when the script loads and runs cleanly.

instruction: Write a script that declares a global string option `mytool_greeting` with default value `hello`, and a command `mytool-greet` that echoes the option's value.
note: The freeform-string option type is `str`, not `string`; `%opt{name}` reads an option's value inside a command body.

instruction: Write a command `mytool-greet` that echoes `hello`, then map it to the F12 function key in normal mode.
note: Function keys are written `<F1>` through `<F12>` with a capital F (lowercase `<f12>` is rejected); the mapped key sequence must end with `<ret>` to run the command.

instruction: Write a script that declares a completions option named `mytool_completions` and adds it to the completers list so it provides insert-mode completion.
note: Register a custom completer with `declare-option completions <name>`, then `set -add buffer completers option=<name>` (option names allow only [a-zA-Z0-9_], so use underscores, not hyphens).
